info.title: rantai-kb API
info.description:
Upload documents, search them, and read back what was found.

Every route under `/v1` needs an API key: send it as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or as `X-API-Key: <key>`. The key decides the tenant, the scopes (`kb:read`, `kb:write`) and, when it is limited, the knowledge bases the caller may see.

get.summary: Liveness and readiness: are the dependencies answering?
get.description:
`GET /health` — the liveness probe. Public: a health check must not need a
key, or an operator cannot use it to find out why the service is not
answering.

503.description: At least one dependency did not answer

get.description: `GET /v1/categories` — the tenant's categories, ordered by name.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

500.description: The store could not be read

400.description: The body has no 'name' or no 'label'

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

500.description: The store could not be written

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

404.description: No such category in this tenant

500.description: The store could not be written

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

404.description: No such category in this tenant

500.description: The store could not be written

get.description:
`GET /v1/documents` — the caller's documents. Needs the `kb:read` scope. A
key bound to some knowledge bases sees only the documents in them.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many documents to return. 1–500; anything else is the default (100).

parameters.name: knowledgeBaseIds
parameters.description: The knowledge bases to list, as a JSON array or a comma-separated list.

parameters.name: externalRef
parameters.description: Only documents with this exact external reference.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

500.description: The store could not be read

post.description:
`POST /v1/documents` — accepts the upload, returns `202` with the document
and job ids. Needs the `kb:write` scope. The answer is `202` because
nothing is indexed yet: a worker picks the job up and the caller polls
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}`.

202.description: The document was accepted and a job was queued

400.description: No file, an unsupported extension, or an unknown knowledge base

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

413.description: The upload is larger than the accepted limit

415.description: The file extension is not on the accepted list

500.description: The store could not be written

502.description: The file could not be stored

get.summary: Read one document and its chunks.
get.description:
`GET /v1/documents/{id}` — one document and its chunks. Needs the
`kb:read` scope. A document outside the caller's tenant, or outside a
limited key's knowledge bases, answers the same 404 as an unknown id.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such document is visible to this key

500.description: A store could not be read

delete.summary: Delete a document, softly or for good.
delete.description:
`DELETE /v1/documents/{id}` — mirrors TS deleteDocument: needs `kb:write`;
soft delete sets `deletedAt` and leaves chunks and the blob alone; hard
delete (`?hard=true`) removes the chunks, then the stored object, then the
row.

parameters.name: hard
parameters.description:
`"true"` removes the chunks, the stored original and the row. Anything
else (or nothing) is the soft delete.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

404.description: No such document is visible to this key

500.description: The store could not be written

patch.description:
`PATCH /v1/documents/{id}` — change a document's metadata. Needs the
`kb:write` scope. Absent members are left alone; `subcategory` set to
`null` clears the column.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

404.description: No such document is visible to this key

500.description: The store could not be written

get.description:
`GET /v1/documents/{id}/assets?key=…` — streams one figure crop. The key
must live under the document's own asset prefix; anything else is the same
404 an unknown document gives, so a key cannot be probed.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description:
The storage key of the figure crop, as `assetKey` in the document's
figures.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such document, or no such asset in it

500.description: The store could not be read

get.summary: The entities and relations extracted for a document.
get.description:
`GET /v1/documents/{id}/intelligence` — entities and relations extracted
for a document.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such document is visible to this key

500.description: The store could not be read

get.description:
`GET /v1/documents/{id}/raw` — streams the stored original. The bytes come
back with the document's own MIME type (or `application/octet-stream` when
the store has none).

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such document is visible to this key, or it has no stored file

500.description: The store could not be read

502.description: The stored file could not be loaded

get.summary: The pages, figures and chunk-to-page map of a document.
get.description:
`GET /v1/documents/{id}/structure`. Visibility is
[`find_visible_document`](crate::routes::find_visible_document): tenant
**and** the key's knowledge-base limit, answering the same 404 as an
unknown id so a limited key cannot probe for documents outside its bases.

200.description: The document's pages, figures and chunk map

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such document is visible to this key

500.description: The store could not be read

get.description:
`GET /v1/events` — server-sent ingest progress for the caller's tenant.
The wire format is the TypeScript one byte for byte: an immediate
`": connected\n\n"`, a `": ping\n\n"` keep-alive every 25 s, and one
`event: <name>\ndata: <json>\n\n` frame per progress update. Only this
tenant's frames are written; another tenant's are dropped without waking
the connection's writer. A key limited to some knowledge bases also drops a
frame that names a document outside them, so the stream does not reveal
progress for a document its other routes answer 404 for.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

500.description: The stream could not be opened

get.summary: The upload formats the service accepts.
get.description:
`GET /v1/formats` — the accepted extensions and the size limit. Public,
like the health probe: a client has to know the accepted list before it
has a key.

200.description: The accepted extensions and the size limit

get.summary: Liveness and readiness, under the versioned path.
get.description:
`GET /v1/health` — the same probe as `GET /health`. A separate handler so
that each path is its own OpenAPI operation; the body is the same one
`/health` returns.

503.description: At least one dependency did not answer

get.description:
`GET /v1/jobs/{id}`. No scope check, matching the TypeScript route: any key
of the tenant can poll its own jobs, which is how the upload UI polls the
job the same key just created.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such job, or its document is not visible to this key

500.description: The store could not be read

post.description:
`POST /v1/jobs/{id}/retry` — only a failed job can be retried (409
otherwise). The row goes back to `pending` with the shape the worker's
claim expects, so the next poll picks it up exactly like a fresh job.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

404.description: No such job, or its document is not visible to this key

409.description: The job is not in the failed state

500.description: The store could not be written

get.description:
`GET /v1/knowledge-bases` — the caller's knowledge bases. Needs the
`kb:read` scope. A key bound to some bases sees only those.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

500.description: The store could not be read

post.description:
`POST /v1/knowledge-bases` — 201 with the created row. Needs the `kb:write`
scope. A base without a name is a 400.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

500.description: The store could not be written

delete.description:
`DELETE /v1/knowledge-bases/{id}` — removes the base and its document
links.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

404.description: No such knowledge base in this tenant

500.description: The store could not be written

patch.description:
`PATCH /v1/knowledge-bases/{id}`. Absent fields are untouched; an empty
body returns the row unchanged.

200.description: The knowledge base, after the patch

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:write scope

404.description: No such knowledge base in this tenant

500.description: The store could not be written

post.summary: Ask a question; get the chunks, the sources and the assembled context.
post.description:
`POST /v1/search` — the retrieval answer. Needs the `kb:read` scope. The
answer carries the chunks, the numbered sources, the assembled context and
the stage timings; `degrades` names the arms that did not run, so an empty
answer is never a silent one.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

500.description: The retrieval pipeline failed

get.summary: List the tables the extractor found.
get.description:
`GET /v1/tables?documentId=…` — the document's tables, current version. A
missing `documentId` lists every table of the tenant: the same scope the
tenant-wide reads use, and the shape a caller needs to discover what it may
query after a search.

parameters.name: documentId
parameters.description:
Only the tables of this document. Without it, every table of the
tenant is listed.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such document is visible to this key, or tables are not configured

500.description: The store could not be read

get.summary: Read one table and its manifest.

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such table is visible to this key, or tables are not configured

500.description: The store could not be read

post.summary: Run a typed query against a table.
post.description:
`POST /v1/tables/{id}/query` — run a typed query and return its rows and
receipt. The body is a typed query, never SQL: columns are checked against
the manifest and values are bound as parameters. A refused query answers
`400` with the [`kb_core::tables::QueryError`] JSON itself, so a client
can react to `unknown_column` (and read `available`) instead of parsing
prose.

400.description: The query was refused; the body is the QueryError

401.description: No key, or a key that does not resolve

403.description: The key lacks the kb:read scope

404.description: No such table is visible to this key, or tables are not configured

500.description: The store could not be read

Agg.description: `kb_core::tables::Agg` — the aggregate functions a query may use.

BoostStatsDto.description:
`stats.boost`: how many returned hits carried a usable field for each
requested boost. A hit without the field kept its base relevance and is
not counted; this is not an error count.

label.description: The category's human label. Required when creating one.

name.description: The category's machine name. Required when creating one.

categories.description: The tenant's categories, ordered by name.

CategoryView.description:
One category on the wire. The TypeScript service sends the row as-is, so
the field names are the column names.

externalRef.description: Additive (R2): the externalRef of the chunk's document, or null.

oneOf.description:
Present only when the engine knows which arms produced this chunk. Omitted
rather than null, so a caller can tell "no arms" from "old server".

tableId.description:
Additive (`TBL-1`): the table a `table_summary`/`table_row` hit belongs
to. Absent for every other chunk type.

tableTitle.description: Additive (`TBL-1`): that table's title, when the answer could resolve it.

ChunkPageRef.description: One text chunk's place in the document.

chunkIndex.description: The chunk's 0-based position in the document.

page.description: 0-based page, or null when the chunk has none (a format without pages).

ColumnInfo.description: `kb_core::tables::ColumnInfo` — one column of a table's manifest.

distinct_count.description: How many distinct values the column has.

role.description: What the column means, which decides what may be computed over it.

sample_values.description: Up to ten frequent distinct values, for non-quantity columns.

unit.description: The unit as written (`Rp juta`, `%`, `ton`); never applied to values.

ColumnRole.description:
`kb_core::tables::ColumnRole` — what a column *means*.

A phone number, a postcode or a year is numeric but never summed, so the
role decides what an aggregate may do with the column.

Confidence.description:
`kb_core::tables::Confidence` — how far the manifest's reading of the table
can be trusted.

chunkIndex.description: The chunk's 0-based position in the document.

id.description: The chunk's id, in the wire form `document_chunk:⟨{bare}⟩`.

page.description: The 0-based page the chunk is on.

section.description: The heading path the chunk sits under.

categories.description: The categories the document is filed under.

chunkCount.description: How many chunks the document has.

fileType.description: The file's type, as the store recorded it.

knowledgeBaseIds.description: The knowledge bases the document belongs to.

subcategory.description: The subcategory, when it has one.

updatedAt.description: When the document was last changed.

chunks.description: The document's chunks, in reading order.

DocumentStructureResponse.description: The response body. camelCase on the wire, like every other `/v1` shape.

chunks.description: The document's chunks and the pages they sit on.

externalRef.description: The caller's own reference for the document, when it has one.

pages.description: The document's pages, by page number.

truncated.description:
True when either read reached its cap: more units may exist than are
listed. False does not prove there are none (an index can always answer
short), it only means the cap was not reached.

DocumentSummary.description: `GET /v1/documents` row, field for field as `listDocuments` selects it.

categories.description: The categories the document is filed under.

externalRef.description: Additive: the caller's opaque document reference, or null.

fileType.description: The file's type, as the store recorded it.

knowledgeBaseIds.description: The knowledge bases the document belongs to.

subcategory.description: The subcategory, when it has one.

EntityView.description: `kb_ports::EntityView` — one entity the graph extracted for a document.

name.description: The entity's name as it appears in the text.

ErrorBody.description:
The body every failing request answers with.

One shape for every status: `{"error": "<message>"}`. The message is the
string the TypeScript service returns, so a client that reads `error` keeps
working.

error.description: What went wrong, in the words the service has always used.

FigureStructure.description:
One figure. `key` is the searchable figure chunk's id when the figure has a
chunk, or the asset key for a figure recorded on the document row alone.

assetKey.description: The blob key of the figure's image.

bbox.description: `[x0, y0, x1, y1]` in page points, from `Document.metadata.figures`.

caption.description: The figure's caption, when it has one.

description.description:
What the picture shows, as the image describer read it (`ING-5`).
Additive; absent for figures from before it existed.

key.description: The figure's chunk id, or its asset key.

ocrText.description:
Text legible in the picture, as the image describer read it (`ING-5`);
null when the picture was not read or shows no text.

page.description: The 0-based page the figure is on.

caption.description: The figure's caption, when it has one.

page.description: The 0-based page the figure is on.

column.description: The column the predicate is on.

value.description:
The value to compare against; an array for `in`, `[low, high]` for
`between`.

extensions.description: The file extensions the upload route accepts, each with its leading dot.

maxFileBytes.description: The largest accepted upload, in bytes.

GlobalArmStatsDto.description: `stats.globalArm`: the communities selected and the chunks contributed.

egress.description: Additive (R3): non-local model-endpoint hosts, sorted and de-duplicated.

ok.description:
True when every dependency answered. False means at least one is down;
the `checks` say which.

tier.description: Additive (R3): the `KB_TIER` preset name, or null when none is set.

jobId.description: The job that will ingest it.

knowledgeBaseIds.description: The knowledge bases the document was filed under.

status.description: Always `processing` — the document is not indexed yet.

entities.description: The entities extracted for the document.

relations.description: The relations extracted for the document.

IntelligenceStats.description: The counts of what the extraction found.

entityTypes.description: How many distinct entity kinds were found.

relationTypes.description: How many distinct relation kinds were found.

JobView.description:
`kb_ports::JobView` — the ingest job as `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` returns it.

camelCase on the wire, like every other `/v1` shape.

attempt.description: How many times the job has been attempted.

documentId.description: The document the job ingests, when it names one.

error.description: The failure message, when the job failed.

etaSeconds.description: Seconds left, when the job can estimate it.

step.description: The step the job is on, when it reports one.

stepCurrent.description: The step the job is on, 1-based.

stepTotal.description: How many steps the job has.

knowledgeBases.description: The knowledge bases the caller may see.

KbSummary.description: One knowledge base, as `GET /v1/knowledge-bases` returns it.

color.description: The base's display colour, when it has one.

description.description: The base's description, when it has one.

documentCount.description: How many live documents the base holds.

name.description: The base's name. Required when creating one.

KnowledgeBaseView.description: The row `prisma.knowledgeBase.create` returns, field for field.

color.description: The base's display colour, when it has one.

description.description: The base's description, when it has one.

tenantId.description: The tenant that owns the base.

updatedAt.description: When the base was last changed.

OkResponse.description:
The body every delete answers with.

One shape for every route that removes something: `{"ok": true}`. A delete
that removed nothing answers `404` instead, so `ok` is always `true` when
it is there at all.

key.description: An output column name or alias.

PageStructure.description:
One page. `number` is 0-based, the same numbering as `ChunkMetadata.page`
and a search chunk's `page`; the page-image key is built from `number + 1`.

hasTextLayer.description:
Whether the PDF page had its own text layer. `None` for a document
ingested before page units recorded it, or a page with no page unit.

imageAssetKey.description: The stored page JPEG's blob key, when ingest recorded that it exists.

ocrText.description:
The page's text when ingest recorded it as OCR output. `None` otherwise,
including for old documents where the origin was not stored.

knowledgeBaseIds.description: The knowledge bases the document belongs to.

subcategory.description: `Some(None)` clears the column; absent leaves it alone.

categories.description: The categories the document is filed under.

fileType.description: The file's type, as the store recorded it.

knowledgeBaseIds.description: The knowledge bases the document belongs to.

subcategory.description: The subcategory, when it has one.

updatedAt.description: When the document was last changed.

document.description: The document's row, after the patch.

ProvenanceArm.description:
`kb_ports::ProvenanceArm` — the arms that produced a search hit.

The wire vocabulary, not the store's: `dense` and `sparse` are the two
scored arms, the rest are the engine phases that add a chunk.

oneOf.description: The query named a column the table does not have.

available.description: The columns the table does have.

oneOf.description: SUM/AVG over a column whose role is not Quantity.

role.description: The column's role, which is why it was refused.

oneOf.description: A plain column in `select` that is neither grouped nor aggregated.
The document's privacy policy forbids this (plain rows, MIN/MAX).
A value could not be compared with the column's kind.

column.description: The column the value was for.

QueryError.description:
`kb_core::tables::QueryError` — why a query was refused before it ran.

Every variant is a `400` at the API, and the JSON is the body, so a client
can react to `unknown_column` (and read `available`) instead of parsing a
prose message.

QueryResult.description:
`kb_core::tables::QueryResult` — the rows a query returned, and the receipt
that lets a caller say exactly how the number was computed.

excluded_derived_rows.description: The derived rows left out of the computation.

rows.description: The rows, each with one value per output column.

rows_matched.description: The rows the query matched before grouping.

suppressed_groups.description: The groups hidden by the document's privacy policy.

truncated.description: True when the row cap or the query's own limit cut the output.

warnings.description: Plain-language caveats about how the number was computed.

RelationView.description:
`kb_ports::RelationView` — one edge of the document's entity graph.

`in` and `out` are the record ids of the edge's endpoints.

in.description: The record id of the entity the edge starts at.

out.description: The record id of the entity the edge ends at.

relation_type.description: The relation's type — the dynamic table the edge lives in.

RetrievalDto.description:
Which retrieval arms produced a chunk, as the response reports it.

**Additive** (step S.1c): Bun does not emit `retrieval`, and every field Bun
does emit is unchanged. `search-parity.sh` deletes `.chunks[].retrieval`
before diffing a Bun answer against a Rust one, because a field only one
implementation produces is not a divergence to fix — see
`docs/rust-cutover.md`.

arms.description: The arms, in a canonical order: `dense`, `sparse`, `neighbour`, `figure`.

rerankScore.description:
The cross-encoder score, when a reranker scored this chunk (ADDITIVE
RET-2). Omitted when no reranker ran, so the no-rerank response is
unchanged. It exists so a floor calibration can sweep thresholds
offline against the same score the server's floor uses.

adaptiveArms.description:
Per-request adaptive arm choice (RET-5). `Some(true)`/`Some(false)`
overrides the server's `KB_ADAPTIVE_ARMS`; absent means "use the server
default", which is off.

boost.description:
Additive (`RET-4`): optional recency/authority boosts. Kept untyped so
a malformed value is this route's 400, not a deserialiser 422.

externalRefs.description:
Additive (`RET-3`): only documents whose `Document.externalRef` is one
of these. An explicit empty list selects nothing.

language.description:
Additive (`RET-3`): only documents whose JSONB metadata `language` key
equals this value.

metadata.description:
Additive (`RET-3`): top-level JSONB metadata predicates. Kept untyped
so an invalid key or a non-scalar value is a 400 from validation rather
than a deserialiser 422.

minScore.description:
Optional relevance floor for this request (RET-2). Overrides the
server's `KB_MIN_SCORE`; absent means "use the server default" (which
is unset unless an operator configured one).

query.description:
Left as raw JSON: the TypeScript route rejects a non-string query with
its own 400, which a typed field would turn into a parser error.

tables.description:
Additive (`TBL-1`): the tables belonging to the documents this answer
named, so a caller can go straight to `POST /v1/tables/{id}/query`
without a second lookup. Omitted when there are none.

SearchStatsDto.description:
The `stats` object of a search response.

Every field of the Bun `HybridSearchStats` is kept, with the same name and
the same meaning, because clients already read them and this service is
meant to be a drop-in for it. `stageTimingsMs` is additive: a client that
has never heard of it keeps working, and a client that reads it gets the
part of the latency that the five legacy fields cannot explain — the arms,
the rerank, the Postgres round trips and the serialisation.

The legacy fields are now measured rather than zeroed, so `embeddingTimeMs`
on the standard path is a number instead of a lie. Milliseconds keep
microsecond resolution: a query-cache hit and a 0.4 ms arm are both "0 ms"
once rounded to an integer, and the difference between them is the whole
reason this exists.

armPlanFallback.description:
True when the adaptive plan returned nothing and the full plan was run
once more. Present only when adaptive mode ran.

oneOf.description:
Additive (`RET-4`): what a recency/authority boost applied. Absent when
the request did not ask for one, so an old client's shape is unchanged.

floorDropped.description: How many hits the floor removed. Absent when no floor ran.

floorScoreKind.description:
Which comparable score the relevance floor used (`"rerank"` or
`"dense"`, ADDITIVE RET-2). Absent when no floor ran, so an old client
sees exactly the Bun shape.

oneOf.description:
Additive (`DEC-5`): what the global community arm did. Present only when
the arm ran (`KB_GLOBAL_ARM` on and an aggregative query), so a server
with the flag off answers exactly the earlier shape. `communities: 0`
means the tenant has no community set — the arm had nothing to say, and
that is not a degrade.

queryClass.description:
The question's class (`"exact"`, `"factual"`, `"structural"`,
`"relational"`, `"aggregative"`, `"topical"`). ADDITIVE RET-5; present
only when adaptive arm choice ran. Absent on a default search so an old
client sees exactly the earlier shape.

skippedArms.description:
The arms adaptive mode did not run, each with the class's reason
(`[{"arm":"pageImage","reason":"exact query"}]`). Empty only when the
plan skipped nothing or a fallback ran the full plan.

totalTimeMs.description: Route entry to just before serialisation, in milliseconds.

oneOf.description:
Additive (`DEC-4`): what the tree arm did. `{"nodes": n, "pages": n}`.
Absent unless the arm ran for a structural query and found something, so
a default search keeps exactly the earlier shape.

as.description: The output name for the aggregate.

column.description: The column to aggregate; absent for `count`.

oneOf.description: A plain column, which must be grouped or aggregated elsewhere.

as.description: The output name for the column.

SelectItem.description:
`kb_core::tables::SelectItem` — one output column: a plain column, or an
aggregate.

JSON: `{"column":"Region"}` or `{"agg":"sum","column":"Revenue","as":"total"}`;
`{"agg":"count"}` with no column counts rows.

SkippedArmDto.description: One arm adaptive mode skipped, as serialised in `stats.skippedArms`.

StageDetailDto.description: Measurements that overlap other stages and so are not part of the sum.

entityArm.description:
Always 0: the entity graph reaches search through the graph arm, not as an
arm of its own. Present so a client that reads it does not lose a field.

globalArm.description:
The global (graph community) arm (`DEC-5`): the scoped community read,
the BM25 selection and the scoped chunk fetch. Zero when the flag is off
or the query is not aggregative.

graphArm.description:
The graph arm, end to end: seed lookup, scoped-graph load or cache hit,
the walk, and the chunk fetch it needs to fuse.

keywordArm.description: The keyword arm's store call on its own.

pageArm.description:
The page-image arm's query embed and page search, concurrent with the
text arms.

queryEmbedCached.description:
True when the query embedding came from the cache rather than the
provider.

vectorArm.description: The vector arm's store call on its own.

visionRerank.description: The live vision rerank of the top page images, inside `pages`.

StageTimingsDto.description:
The per-stage breakdown, in milliseconds.

The top level is a *partition* of the request: the stages there run one
after another and add up to no more than [`SearchStatsDto::total_time_ms`].
`detail` is the overlapping part — the query embed and the two arms all
happen inside `arms`, so they are reported, never summed with it.

arms.description: The concurrent retrieval phase: query embed + both arms.

context.description: Building the context string and the numbered sources.

detail.description: The overlapping measurements, reported for diagnosis only.

enrich.description: Alive check and title/category enrichment on the hits that survived.

pages.description: Page-image arm after the text rerank: page fusion and page rerank.

scopeBuild.description: `build_scope` in Postgres: which documents this caller may see.

total.description:
Route entry to just before serialisation. The sum of everything above
is bounded by it.

TableDto.description:
A table as the API returns it: the record with its manifest, camelCase like
the rest of this API.

`gridKey` is the caller's own blob key. It is included because the record is
the contract and an operator debugging a stored table needs it; it names no
other tenant's data.

caption.description: The table's caption, when it has one.

documentId.description: The document the table came from.

gridKey.description: The blob key of the table's stored grid.

index.description: The table's position in the document.

manifest.description: What the manifest's own reading of the table can be trusted to mean.

pageSpan.description: The pages the table spans, as `[first, last]`.

sheet.description: The sheet the table was on, for spreadsheets.

tenantId.description: The tenant that owns the table.

title.description: The table's title, when it has one.

TableManifest.description:
`kb_core::tables::TableManifest` — what the manifest's own reading of a
table can be trusted to mean.

columns.description: One entry per column, in the table's own order.

confidence.description: How far the manifest can be trusted.

formulas_known.description: True when the derived rows are proven by formulas rather than guessed.

n_cols.description: How many columns the table has.

n_rows.description: How many data rows the table has.

notes.description: Extraction notes carried forward ("hidden sheet skipped", …).

truncated.description: True when rows were dropped to fit the extractor's row cap.

TableQuery.description:
`kb_core::tables::TableQuery` — the typed query
`POST /v1/tables/{id}/query` accepts. Never SQL: columns are checked
against the manifest and values are bound as parameters.

include_derived.description: Count subtotal/total rows too (off by default: they double-count).

limit.description: The maximum number of rows to return.

select.description: The output columns, plain or aggregated.

TableRefDto.description: One table named by a search answer (`TBL-1`). Additive.

TreeArmStatsDto.description:
`stats.treeArm`: outline nodes the query scored and the distinct pages the
arm read. Not a latency figure; the counts say how much structure the
question actually reached.

UploadForm.description:
The multipart form `POST /v1/documents` accepts.

The file is the part named `file`; every other part is a text field. The
schema names them all — with the names the form really uses, camelCase
included — so a reader of the spec knows the whole form without reading
the route.

categories.description:
The categories the document is filed under, as a JSON array or a
comma-separated list.

documentType.description: The kind of document, as the extractor should read it.

externalRef.description: The caller's own reference for this document.

figures.description: How hard to look for figures: `auto`, `all`, `none` or `off`.

file.description: The document itself. Its extension decides whether it is accepted.

knowledgeBaseIds.description:
The knowledge bases to file the document under, as a JSON array or a
comma-separated list. Ids the tenant does not own are a 400.

metadata.description:
A JSON object of extra metadata, stored as the document's JSONB
metadata and read by the `metadata` search filter.

subcategory.description: The subcategory, when the document has one.

tablePrivacy.description:
`aggregate-only` restricts this document's tables to whole-group
aggregates; `open` (the default) leaves them open.

title.description: The document's title. Defaults to the file name without its extension.

bearer_auth.description: The API key, as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`. The scheme is matched case-insensitively.

tags.name: documents
tags.description: Upload documents, list them, read one, and change or delete it.

tags.name: search
tags.description: Ask a question and get the chunks, the numbered sources and the assembled context.

tags.name: jobs
tags.description: Follow an ingest job's progress and requeue a failed one.

tags.name: tables
tags.description: List the tables a document's extractor found and query them with a typed query.

tags.name: taxonomy
tags.description: Knowledge bases and categories: the labels documents are filed under.

tags.name: structure
tags.description: The pages, figures and chunk-to-page map of one document.

tags.name: media
tags.description: The stored original, the figure crops and the entities extracted for a document.

tags.name: health
tags.description: Liveness, readiness and the accepted upload formats. No key needed.
